key_insight: The paper shows that a deterministic trajectory can be made robust in a distribution-agnostic way by learning an affine feedback correction policy under chance constraints, without needing to assume a specific uncertainty model.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical template for mission design under uncertain dynamics, letting engineers preserve feasibility and competitive fuel performance across very different trajectory-planning problems.
method: Compute a nominal offline trajectory as the baseline.
Use reinforcement learning to learn feedforward control corrections and time-varying feedback gains.
Enforce probabilistic feasibility with rollout-based upper-tail quantiles and terminal dispersion penalties.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on two diverse problems—3D multi-impulse Earth-Mars transfer and stochastic atmospheric rocket landing—and tested under Gaussian, bounded uniform, and unseen disturbance conditions.
watch_item: Performance depends on sampled rollouts and empirical quantiles, so reliability may be sensitive to sampling quality, training coverage, and unseen uncertainty extremes.
paper_title: Distribution-Agnostic Robust Trajectory Optimization via Chance-Constrained Reinforcement Learning
